channel.title: Bay Area Sports Blog
channel.description: Every Bay Area team, argued about properly. The 49ers, Warriors, Giants, A's and Sharks, written by a fan, not a network.

item.title: 49ers 41, Chargers 17: The Best Night of the Summer
item.description: 49ers 41, Chargers 17 at SoFi: Jacob Cowing took a punt 83 yards, the run game piled up 146, and San Francisco led Harbaugh's Chargers 20 to 3 at the half.

item.title: Royals 9, Athletics 7: A Seven Run Eighth Buried Them
item.description: Royals 9, Athletics 7: the A's led 5-1 in the eighth in Kansas City and the Royals scored seven. Second blown late lead in two nights. 49-78.

item.title: Giants 1, Guardians 0: One Run Was Enough for Once
item.description: Giants 1, Guardians 0: Houser and Dylan Smith threw seven scoreless in Cleveland, a Bericoto ground ball scored the only run, and Messick struck out ten in a loss.

item.title: Royals 4, A's 3: A Two Run Ninth Inning Lead, Gone in Ten Minutes
item.description: Royals 4, Athletics 3 at Kauffman Stadium: the A's led 3-1 into the ninth, Hogan Harris gave up three, Bobby Witt Jr. walked it off, and the A's fall to 49-77.

item.title: Barry Bonds and the Giants: The Years, the Numbers, the Argument
item.description: Barry Bonds played fifteen seasons for the Giants and hit 586 of his 762 home runs here. The 73 home run year, the 2002 World Series, and the argument.

item.title: Cal Football Schedule 2026: Every Game, Date, Time and TV
item.description: The full Cal Golden Bears 2026 football schedule: every game, date, kickoff time and TV network, from the UCLA opener to the Big Game on 21 November.

item.title: Cal Basketball Schedule 2026-27: Every Game Announced
item.description: The Cal basketball schedule for 2026-27: the announced non conference games, every ACC opponent home and away, and the 2025-26 results for reference.

item.title: Guardians 8, Giants 1: Eldridge Homered, Nothing Else Happened
item.description: Guardians 8, Giants 1 in Cleveland: Bryce Eldridge homered for his 14th, Jo Adell drove in six, and one run was the entire Giants offense. They are 51-74.

item.title: Josuar Gonzalez Is the Best Giants Prospect in a Generation
item.description: Josuar Gonzalez is 18, a switch-hitting shortstop ranked as high as seventh in baseball, and he is hitting .339 at Low-A San Jose. Why Giants fans should care.

item.title: San Jose Sharks Playoff History: Every Run, Year by Year
item.description: The complete San Jose Sharks playoff history: all 21 postseason trips, the 1994 upset, the 2016 Stanley Cup Final, the 2019 comeback and the drought since.

item.title: Warriors Projected Rotation 2026-27: Who Actually Plays
item.description: Our projected Warriors rotation for 2026-27: the ten men who play, the minutes each should get, who closes, and what changes when Jimmy Butler is back.

item.title: Warriors Depth Chart 2026-27: Every Position, Explained
item.description: The Warriors depth chart for 2026-27: the projected starters, the bench behind them, where Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody fit, and where this roster runs out.

item.title: When Were the San Jose Sharks Founded? The Full Origin Story
item.description: The San Jose Sharks were founded on 9 May 1990 and began play in 1991-92. The Gund brothers, the North Stars swap, the Cow Palace years and how they got the name.

item.title: They Took Brandon Aiyuk's Locker Out. That Is How You Know It Is Over.
item.description: Brandon Aiyuk's locker stall is gone from the 49ers locker room. It survived all of last season after he left the team. Now the standoff is basically over.

item.title: McCaffrey Is Not Practicing, and It Might Not Be About a Muscle
item.description: Christian McCaffrey has not practiced at 49ers camp, no injury attached, and the running back market just moved. Nick Bosa has not been out there either.

item.title: Vitello Called It Junior High Baseball. Posey Says He Is Back.
item.description: Tony Vitello called the Giants loss to the Rockies a junior high performance, and Buster Posey has confirmed he is back next year. Both of those are a problem.

item.title: Harbaugh Comes Back Thursday, and Kittle Finally Sounds Like Himself
item.description: The 49ers play Harbaugh's Chargers at SoFi on Thursday night, and George Kittle says his Achilles recovery is hitting every marker with Week 1 in reach.

item.title: Rockies 13, Giants 7: Devers Hit His 25th and It Did Not Matter
item.description: Rockies 13, Giants 7 at Oracle Park: Rafael Devers homered for his 25th, the Giants led into the sixth, and the bullpen gave up seven unanswered to Colorado.

item.title: They Called De'Zhaun Stribling a Reach. Nobody Is Laughing Now
item.description: Draft night said the 49ers reached for De'Zhaun Stribling. One camp and one preseason game later, that take has aged like milk.

item.title: The 49ers Finally Have the Mix Right, and the Drafts Are Why
item.description: A veteran core in its prime, smart short-term signings, and draft picks who actually play. The 49ers roster balance is the best it has been in years.

item.title: Giants 7, Rockies 1: Logan Webb Is the Consummate Pro
item.description: Giants 7, Rockies 1 at Oracle Park: Logan Webb went six innings with no walks and seven strikeouts, Drew Gilbert drove in three, and a six-run fourth ended it.

item.title: The 49ers Sat Everybody. The Raiders Played Everybody and Lost Worse.
item.description: Preseason week one recap: Shanahan sat every 49ers starter in a 19-13 loss, Rourke and Stribling impressed, and the Raiders lost 27-14 at home.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan Needs to Win the Ring This Year. Say It Out Loud.
item.description: Year ten of Kyle Shanahan, two Super Bowl losses, a peaking Brock Purdy and a loaded roster: why 2026 is the season the ring becomes the whole job.

item.title: The Warriors Cling to the Past Because They Cannot Build a Future
item.description: Wiseman, the two timelines, Poole, Kuminga, Moody: why the Warriors keep buying old veterans, because this franchise cannot develop young players.

item.title: The 49ers Waived Junior Bergen Again, and Kept the Punter
item.description: The 49ers waived Junior Bergen and Jack Bouwmeester and put K.J. Henry on waived/injured, then signed Eli Apple, Xavier Thomas and Zamir White.

item.title: Rays 12, A's 4: Six Home Runs, Two of Them From a .216 Hitter
item.description: Tampa Bay hit six home runs in a 12-4 win at Sutter Health Park and Nick Martinez threw a complete game. The A's fall to 47-73 and lose another series.

item.title: Astros 2, Giants 1: Six Shutout Innings, One Drop, One Bad Back
item.description: Astros 2, Giants 1 at Oracle Park: Adrian Houser's six shutout innings wasted, a Bericoto error tied it, and Willy Adames left with back spasms.

item.title: Giants 4, Astros 1: Carson Whisenhunt Was Worth the Wait
item.description: Carson Whisenhunt outpitched Hunter Brown in a 4-1 win at Oracle Park. Eldridge homered, Cavanaugh and Koss drove in runs, and the Giants got to fifty wins.

item.title: Four Running Backs Down, Bosa Sore, and Kittle Running. Again.
item.description: McCaffrey out with tightness, the three backs behind him hurt, tryouts for Nyheim Miller-Hines and Zamir White, Bosa sore, and Kittle running again.

item.title: A's 4, Red Sox 3: A Series Win, Their First Since Mid-June
item.description: Max Muncy's ninth-inning double off Aroldis Chapman beat Boston 4-3 and gave the Athletics their first series win since mid-June, plus McNeil's 1,000th hit.

item.title: Don Nelson Dies at 86: Nellie Ball, Run TMC and What He Gave Us
item.description: Don Nelson died 9 August 2026 at 86. The coach who invented the point forward, built Run TMC, coached We Believe and handed the ball to a rookie Stephen Curry.

item.title: Tigers 3, Giants 1 (F/10): We Wasted Eight Innings of Logan Webb
item.description: Logan Webb threw eight innings and allowed no earned runs, and the Giants still lost 3-1 in ten to Detroit. Seven hits, seven left on, twenty games under.

item.title: The Defense Won Saturday. Shanahan Coaches Thursday.
item.description: The 49ers defense got the better of Brock Purdy on Saturday, and Kyle Shanahan will be coaching the sideline himself in the preseason opener against Tennessee.

item.title: Roupp Showed Up Vitello, and That Is the Whole Season
item.description: Landen Roupp glared at Tony Vitello and waved him off in the Giants' 8-0 loss to Detroit. It says everything about a manager this clubhouse has stopped playing for.

item.title: The 2026 49ers Roster and Depth Chart, Position by Position
item.description: A position-by-position look at the 2026 49ers roster: starters, key backups, the injury situation, and where the depth actually runs out.

item.title: The 2026 49ers Schedule, Week by Week
item.description: The 2026 49ers schedule with the structure that matters: the Melbourne opener, the Mexico City game, five prime-time slots, and our coverage of each week.

item.title: The 2026 49ers: Roster, Schedule, and the Questions That Decide It
item.description: A structural preview of the 2026 49ers: the offense, the defence, the coaching, the schedule, and the four questions that actually decide the year.

item.title: The NFL Is Opening the 49ers Season in Melbourne. Really.
item.description: The 49ers open 2026 against the Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, the NFL's first regular season game in Australia. What that costs in Week 1.

item.title: Andrew Luck Is Running a Football Program. It Is Working.
item.description: Stanford handed Andrew Luck a general manager job nobody else in college football has. Here is why the structure matters more than the name on it.

item.title: The Athletics Roster and Depth Chart
item.description: A position-by-position look at the Athletics roster: the young core, the rotation, and which players are likely to still be here in 2028.
